title: Sample preparation method for large scale shear testing of soft-clay and granular-column composites
author: Cengiz, Guler

steps.title: Assemble drainage pipe and rig
steps.instruction: Install the drainage pipe assembly on the base, fit all sealing components, and prepare the consolidation chambers for slurry placement.

substeps.instruction: Place the concentric stainless‑steel drainage pipe assembly into the 50 mm‑deep machined groove at the base of the rig.
Engage the two O‑ring bearing grooves on the pipe periphery with the base and apply high‑vacuum grease to the O‑rings to prevent leakage.
Fit a rubber gasket around both the outer periphery and the inner opening of the doughnut‑shaped surcharge plate to seal the clay bed.
Ensure the four guide rods extending from the square flange keep the surcharge plate vertical and prevent twisting during loading.
Secure the four steel rods that transfer the downward force from the pneumatic actuator to the surcharge plate while leaving a clearance for the drainage pipe.
Grease the inner periphery of each of the four 460 mm‑inner‑diameter consolidation chambers and the outer surface of the drainage pipe to reduce side friction.

steps.title: Prepare perforated pipe openings
steps.instruction: Cover the perforations of the outer pipe to keep them free of grease while still allowing water flow.

substeps.instruction: Cover the perforations (arranged in four vertical alignments) on the outer 113 mm‑OD pipe with filter paper.
Place a single line of tape over the filter paper to prevent grease from entering the perforations.
After greasing the pipe (see previous step), carefully remove the tape line.

steps.title: Fill annular water pool
steps.instruction: Create a water pool between the concentric pipes to keep the slurry fully inundated during consolidation.

substeps.instruction: Insert the inner non‑perforated pipe (50 mm OD) into the outer perforated pipe (113 mm OD) so the inner pipe extends slightly beyond the outer pipe.
Fill the annular cavity between the two pipes flush with tap water, forming a continuous water pool.
Verify that excess water can drip from the inner pipe to a collection dish during consolidation.

steps.title: Prepare and mix clay slurry
steps.instruction: Produce a kaolinite clay slurry at the required water content and deliver it to the consolidation chambers.

substeps.instruction: Add water to a mixing tank.
Add powdered kaolinite clay to achieve a water content of 75 % (1.5 × the liquid limit of the clay).
Mix thoroughly to avoid lump formation.
Elevate the tank with an overhead crane.
Open the tank outlet and allow the slurry to flow by gravity into the four consolidation chambers, filling bottom‑up to prevent trapped air bubbles.

steps.title: Install surcharge plate and apply load
steps.instruction: Place the surcharge plate on the slurry surface and incrementally apply vertical surcharge pressures using the pneumatic actuator.

substeps.instruction: Position the doughnut‑shaped surcharge plate on top of the clay slurry surface and secure it to the surcharge assembly.
Connect the 160 mm‑diameter pneumatic piston (700 mm stroke) to the assembly.
Use a precision air regulator to incrementally increase air flow to the actuator; monitor pressure with an air‑pressure sensor linked to a digital gauge.
With a maximum available air pressure of 800 kPa, apply up to 100 kPa vertical surcharge pressure on the clay bed.
Consolidate the clay beds sequentially to the target overburden pressures of 30 kPa, 45 kPa, 60 kPa, 75 kPa, and 90 kPa.
